request.spec:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person now shows a settled-total and an open-total, and the sheet shows both added up across everyone. All 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

The change is all in `src/main/frontend/features/rates/rates.slot.tsx`:

- **Built from the due-total's own loop.** I reworked the function that adds up each person's due-total so it also keeps a settled part and an open part. Both totals therefore leave out exactly the claims the due-total leaves out (held, deferred, retired-and-excluded). The two always add up to the person's due-total before the cap.
- **Per person.** Settled-total adds the due of their SETTLED claims, which is the figure fixed at settling, corrections included. Open-total adds their OPEN and PENDING claims. They sit next to the due-total as `person-settled-total` and `person-open-total`.
- **Sheet.** `rollup-settled-total` and `rollup-open-total` sit right after the sheet's due-total. They are plain sums, without the highest-and-lowest trim the sheet's due-total applies.

When a person's due-total shows `n/a`, these two still show numbers, counting a claim with no figure as 0. The spec never checks that case, so it's a choice I made.

No server, database or audit changes were needed. The spec expects no new audit fields.
